item.title: Forecasters are predicting a warmer and wetter winter. Here's how El Niño will affect your region
item.description: El Niño years typically lead to more precipitation and higher-than-average temperatures. The latest data shows the different potential impacts by region.

item.description: The Trump administration wants to undo a Biden-era rule that would reduce methane emissions from the oil and gas industry.

item.description: President Donald Trump said that his administration is "terminating" a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut planet-warming emissions of methane from oil and gas drilling.

item.title: Flooding in Four Corners region displaces residents, as storms move southeast
item.description: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.

item.title: Europe's heat claims 50,000 lives. Climate change blamed for two-thirds of deaths
item.description: Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.
item.content:encoded:

item.description: The United Nations warns that countries are not meeting their goals to limit warming and avoid the worst consequences of climate change.

item.title: Meet the people moving north to escape increasingly hot summers
item.description: As climate change fuels hotter summers, some Britons are moving north in search of cooler weather. Could a similar shift be on the horizon in the United States?

item.title: United Nations report highlights significant increase in U.S. climate pollution
item.description: The U.S. is the only major economy where planet-warming pollution dramatically increased last year. The United Nations warns the planet is on track for catastrophic warming.

item.title: A Kelvin wave raised sea levels on the West Coast. More are coming
item.description: A large underwater wave moved up the West Coast, raising sea levels. Scientists say it's driven by El Niño and it's going to happen again.
